title: BEYOND STRUCTURE: INVARIANT CRYSTAL PROPERTY PREDICTION WITH PSEUDO-PARTICLE RAY DIFFRACTION
research_summary: Crystal property prediction, governed by quantum mechanical principles, is computationally prohibitive to solve exactly for large many-body systems using traditional density functional theory. While machine learning models have emerged as efficient approximations for large-scale applications, their performance is strongly influenced by the choice of atomic representation. Although modern graph-based approaches have progressively incorporated more structural information, they often fail to capture long-range atomic interactions due to finite receptive fields and local encoding schemes. This limitation leads to distinct crystals being mapped to identical representations, hindering accurate property prediction. To address this, we introduce PRDNet that leverages unique reciprocal-space diffraction besides graph representations. To enhance sensitivity to elemental and environmental variations, we employ a data-driven pseudo-particle to generate a synthetic diffraction pattern. PRDNet ensures full invariance to crystallographic symmetries. Extensive experiments are conducted on Materials Project, JARVIS-DFT, and MatBench, demonstrating that the proposed model achieves state-of-the-art performance.

title: A SINGLE ARCHITECTURE FOR REPRESENTING INVARIANCE UNDER ANY SPACE GROUP
research_summary: This paper introduces the Crystal Fourier Transformer (CFT), a single neural architecture that adapts its weights to enforce exact invariance to any of the 230 crystallographic space groups. It achieves this by analytically deriving constraints that group operations impose on Fourier coefficients, encoding these constraints into a group-conditional routing matrix (adjacency matrix of a dual graph), and using it to transform standard Fourier positional encodings into symmetry-adapted ones. The method enables weight sharing across all space groups, improves generalization on sparse data, and supports zero-shot learning for unseen groups.

title: Accurate prediction of tensorial spectra using equivariant graph neural network
research_summary: Here we introduce the Tensorial Spectra Equivariant Neural Network (TSENN), an equivariant graph neural network architecture that maps crystal structures directly to their full photon-frequency-dependent optical tensors. By encoding isotropic sequential scalar components and anisotropic sequential tensor components into spherical tensor representations, TSENN ensures symmetry-aware predictions consistent with crystalline symmetry constraints. Trained on frequency-dependent dielectric tensors of 1,432 bulk semiconductors, the model achieves a mean absolute error of 0.127, demonstrating its potential for efficient and general modeling of optical properties.

title: A framework to evaluate machine learning crystal stability predictions
research_summary: We present Matbench Discovery as an example evaluation framework for machine learning energy models, here applied as pre-filters to first-principles computed data in a high-throughput search for stable inorganic crystals.

title: Predicting thermodynamic stability of inorganic compounds using ensemble machine learning based on electron configuration
research_summary: This paper proposes an ensemble machine learning framework—Electron Configuration models with Stacked Generalization (ECSG)—to predict the thermodynamic stability of inorganic compounds. ECSG integrates three base-level models grounded in distinct domain knowledge: electron configuration (via ECCNN), atomic properties (Magpie), and interatomic interactions (Roost). The framework achieves high predictive accuracy (AUC = 0.988 on JARVIS) and exceptional sample efficiency (requiring only 1/7 the data of existing models). It is validated across multiple databases (MP, OQMD, JARVIS), unknown composition spaces (perovskite halides, Li-containing oxides, transition metal oxides), and applied in two case studies: discovery of 2D wide bandgap semiconductors and double perovskite oxides—both confirmed via first-principles calculations.

title: Transformer-generated atomic embeddings to enhance prediction accuracy of crystal properties with machine learning
research_summary: This paper proposes a novel atomic embedding strategy called universal atomic embeddings (UAEs), generated by a custom-built CrystalTransformer model based on the Transformer architecture. The ct-UAEs are designed as broadly applicable atomic fingerprints that capture complex atomic features more effectively than traditional methods (e.g., one-hot encoding). Evaluated on formation energy and bandgap prediction across multiple databases (Materials Project, JARVIS, MC3D, hybrid perovskites), ct-UAEs consistently improve prediction accuracy—e.g., 14% MAE reduction for formation energy in CGCNN—and demonstrate strong transferability and interpretability via clustering and property correlation analysis.

title: Hierarchy-boosted funnel learning for identifying semiconductors with ultralow lattice thermal conductivity
research_summary: The paper proposes a hierarchy-boosted funnel learning (HiBoFL) framework that integrates unsupervised and supervised learning to efficiently identify semiconductors with ultralow lattice thermal conductivity (κL), circumventing large-scale brute-force ab initio calculations. It uses unsupervised clustering on a high-throughput Materials Project dataset to narrow the search space, performs low-cost phonon-elasticity-thermal (PET) model-based high-throughput calculations on selected clusters to build a labeled local database, trains an interpretable CatBoost classifier to predict ultralow κL, and discovers a new structural descriptor (Lmin) governing structural anharmonicity and phonon lifetime.

title: LLM-Prop: predicting the properties of crystalline materials using large language models
research_summary: The paper introduces LLM-Prop, a method that leverages large language models (LLMs) to predict physical and electronic properties of crystalline materials from their natural language text descriptions—bypassing traditional graph-based representations. It proposes a benchmark dataset (TextEdge), develops a fine-tuned T5 encoder architecture with specialized preprocessing (e.g., [NUM]/[ANG] tokenization, [CLS] prepending, label scaling), and demonstrates superior performance over state-of-the-art GNNs and domain-specific LLMs (e.g., MatBERT) on six crystal properties including band gap, unit cell volume, formation energy, and band gap type classification.

title: RETHINKING THE ROLE OF FRAMES FOR SE(3)-INVARIANT CRYSTAL STRUCTURE MODELING
research_summary: This paper proposes 'dynamic frames' for SE(3)-invariant crystal structure modeling, challenging the conventional use of static, structure-aligned frames. Dynamic frames are constructed per atom and per message-passing layer using learned attention weights to reflect local interatomic interactions, rather than global structural symmetry. The concept is implemented in CrystalFramer, a transformer-based architecture extending Crystalformer, and evaluated on crystal property prediction tasks across JARVIS, Materials Project, and OQMD datasets.

title: A Denoising Pre-training Framework for Accelerating Novel Material Discovery
research_summary: The paper introduces an unsupervised Denoising Pre-training Framework (DPF) for crystal structures to overcome the scarcity of labeled data in crystal property prediction. DPF trains models to reconstruct original crystal structures by recovering masked atom types, perturbed atom positions, and perturbed lattice constants. It pre-trains on 380,743 unlabeled crystal structures and fine-tunes on downstream property prediction tasks, demonstrating improved performance across multiple benchmarks.

title: PDDFormer: Pairwise Distance Distribution Graph Transformer for Crystal Material Property Prediction
research_summary: The paper introduces WPDDFormer and UPDDFormer—graph transformer models that integrate atom-weighted and unit-cell pairwise distance distribution (PDD) representations into multi-edge crystal graphs to achieve continuous and geometrically complete crystal structure representations, enabling improved prediction of material properties such as formation energy, band gap, bulk modulus, and shear modulus on Materials Project and JARVIS-DFT benchmarks.

title: Accelerating materials property prediction via a hybrid Transformer Graph framework that leverages four body interactions
research_summary: We propose a framework utilizing a Graph Neural Network with composition-based and crystal structure-based architectures, combined with a transfer learning scheme. This approach accurately predicts energy-related properties (e.g., total energy, energy above the convex hull, energy band gap) and data-scarce mechanical properties (e.g., bulk and shear modulus). Our model incorporates four-body interactions, capturing periodicity and structural characteristics. It outperforms state-of-the-art models in 8 materials property regression tasks.

title: Cross-scale covariance for material property prediction
research_summary: A simulation can stand its ground against an experiment only if its prediction uncertainty is known. The unknown accuracy of interatomic potentials (IPs) is a major source of prediction uncertainty, severely limiting the use of large-scale classical atomistic simulations in a wide range of scientiﬁc and engineering applications. Here we explore covariance between predictions of metal plasticity, from 178 large-scale (~108 atoms) molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and a variety of indicator properties computed at small-scales (≤102 atoms). All simulations use the same 178 IPs. In a manner similar to statistical studies in public health, we analyze correlations of strength with indicators, identify the best predictor properties, and build a cross-scale “strength-on-predictors” regression model. This model is then used to estimate regression error over the statistical pool of IPs. Small-scale predictors found to be highly covariant with strength are computed using expensive quantum-accurate calculations and used to predict ﬂow strength, within the statistical error bounds established in our study.

title: Advancing extrapolative predictions of material properties through learning to learn using extrapolative episodic training
research_summary: This study develops a meta-learning methodology—extrapolative episodic training (E2T)—to enhance the ability of machine learning models to predict material properties outside the domain of training data. Using attention-based matching neural networks (MNNs) trained on arbitrarily generated extrapolative episodes, the method demonstrates superior generalization for unseen material domains, particularly in predicting physical properties of polymeric materials and hybrid organic–inorganic perovskites. The approach enables rapid adaptation to new domains with limited data via fine-tuning, outperforming conventional supervised learning and state-of-the-art baselines like ANE in extrapolative settings.

title: Probing out-of-distribution generalization in machine learning for materials
research_summary: This paper systematically evaluates the out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization capabilities of various machine learning models across over 700 OOD tasks derived from large materials datasets (JARVIS, Materials Project, OQMD). It challenges heuristic definitions of OOD tasks—based on chemistry (e.g., leave-one-element-out) or structural symmetry (e.g., leave-one-space-group-out)—by revealing that most such tasks are not truly extrapolative but rather represent interpolation within the high-dimensional materials representation space. Using UMAP-based domain identification and kernel-density estimation, the authors distinguish statistically OOD from representationally OOD test data. They find that robust OOD performance is common—even for simple models like XGBoost—and that poor performance is concentrated in a few cases (e.g., H, F, O compounds) where test data lie outside the training domain. Crucially, neural scaling laws (increasing training size/time improves performance) hold only for representationally in-domain OOD tasks; for representationally OOD tasks, scaling often degrades performance. The work concludes that current OOD benchmarks overestimate generalizability and calls for rigorously challenging, physically meaningful OOD benchmarks.

title: Known Unknowns: Out-of-Distribution Property Prediction in Materials and Molecules
research_summary: Our objective is to train predictor models that extrapolate zero-shot to higher ranges than in the training data, given the chemical compositions of solids or molecular graphs and their property values. We propose using a transductive approach to OOD property prediction, achieving improvements in prediction accuracy. In particular, our method improves extrapolative precision by 1.8× for materials and 1.5× for molecules, and boosts recall of high-performing candidates by up to 3×. Our method leverages analogical input-target relations in the training and test sets, enabling generalization beyond the training target support, and can be applied to any other material and molecular tasks.

title: Dielectric tensor prediction for inorganic materials using latent information from preferred potential
research_summary: This study develops DTNet, an equivariant neural network that leverages pretrained multi-rank structural embeddings from the universal neural network potential PFP to predict total, electronic, and ionic dielectric tensors for inorganic materials across 72 elements. It benchmarks performance against state-of-the-art models and conducts virtual screening on thermodynamically stable Materials Project candidates to discover high-dielectric and highly anisotropic materials, experimentally validating top candidates via DFPT.

title: A Space Group Symmetry Informed Network for O(3) Equivariant Crystal Tensor Prediction
research_summary: We consider the prediction of general tensor properties of crystalline materials, including dielectric, piezoelectric, and elastic tensors. A key challenge here is how to make the predictions satisfy the unique tensor equivariance to O(3) group and invariance to crystal space groups. To this end, we propose a General Materials Tensor Network (GMTNet), which is carefully designed to satisfy the required symmetries. To evaluate our method, we curate a dataset and establish evaluation metrics that are tailored to the intricacies of crystal tensor predictions. Experimental results show that our GMTNet not only achieves promising performance on crystal tensors of various orders but also generates predictions fully consistent with the intrinsic crystal symmetries.

title: COMPLETE AND EFFICIENT GRAPH TRANSFORMERS FOR CRYSTAL MATERIAL PROPERTY PREDICTION
research_summary: Crystal structures are characterized by atomic bases within a primitive unit cell that repeats along a regular lattice throughout 3D space. The periodic and infinite nature of crystals poses unique challenges for geometric graph representation learning. Specifically, constructing graphs that effectively capture the complete geometric information of crystals and handle chiral crystals remains an unsolved and challenging problem. In this paper, we introduce a novel approach that utilizes the periodic patterns of unit cells to establish the lattice-based representation for each atom, enabling efficient and expressive graph representations of crystals. Furthermore, we propose ComFormer, a SE(3) transformer designed specifically for crystalline materials.

title: CRYSTALFORMER: INFINITELY CONNECTED ATTENTION FOR PERIODIC STRUCTURE ENCODING
research_summary: Predicting physical properties of materials from their crystal structures is a fundamental problem in materials science. In this work, we show that this infinitely connected attention can lead to a computationally tractable formulation, interpreted as neural potential summation, that performs infinite interatomic potential summations in a deeply learned feature space. We then propose a simple yet effective Transformer-based encoder architecture for crystal structures called Crystalformer.

title: A Diffusion-Based Pre-training Framework for Crystal Property Prediction
research_summary: The paper proposes CrysDiff, a diffusion-based pretrain-finetune framework to address data scarcity in crystal property prediction. It pre-trains on abundant unlabeled 3D crystal structures via self-supervised crystal structure reconstruction (diffusing and denoising lattice L and fractional coordinates F), then fine-tunes on sparse labeled data to predict target properties (e.g., formation energy, bandgap). The method enforces crystal symmetries (O(3) invariance, periodic translation invariance) using an EGNN-based denoising model throughout both phases.

title: Structure-aware graph neural network based deep transfer learning framework for enhanced predictive analytics on diverse materials datasets
research_summary: This paper presents a structure-aware graph neural network (GNN) based deep transfer learning framework to improve predictive performance for materials properties using sparse data. It leverages the ALIGNN architecture trained on large source datasets (e.g., Materials Project formation energy) and applies transfer learning—via fine-tuning or feature extraction—to small target datasets across diverse materials classes (3D/2D, inorganic/organic, computational/experimental). The framework is evaluated on 115 dataset-property combinations, showing TL models outperform scratch-trained models in ≈90% of cases, especially for extrapolation and small-data regimes.

title: Higher-order equivariant neural networks for charge density prediction in materials
research_summary: We introduce ChargE3Net, an E(3)-equivariant graph neural network for predicting electron density in atomic systems. ChargE3Net enables the learning of higher-order equivariant features to achieve high predictive accuracy and model expressivity. We show that ChargE3Net exceeds the performance of prior work on diverse sets of molecules and materials. When trained on the massive dataset of over 100K materials in the Materials Project database, our model is able to capture the complexity and variability in the data, leading to a significant 26.7% reduction in self-consistent iterations when used to initialize DFT calculations on unseen materials. Furthermore, we show that non-self-consistent DFT calculations using our predicted charge densities yield near-DFT performance on electronic and thermodynamic property prediction at a fraction of the computational cost.

title: MD-HIT: Machine learning for material property prediction with dataset redundancy control
research_summary: This paper addresses the problem of overestimated machine learning model performance in materials science due to dataset redundancy—i.e., highly similar materials in training and test sets causing information leakage. It proposes MD-HIT, a redundancy reduction algorithm inspired by bioinformatics' CD-HIT, with two variants: MD-HIT-composition (using composition-based distance metrics like Mendeleev and MatScholar) and MD-HIT-structure (using structure-based metrics like XRD and OFM features). The authors apply MD-HIT to Materials Project datasets for formation energy and band gap prediction, demonstrating that redundancy-controlled splits yield lower but more realistic and generalizable (especially out-of-distribution) ML performance compared to standard random splits.

title: Virtual Node Graph Neural Network for Full Phonon Prediction
research_summary: The paper introduces the Virtual Node Graph Neural Network (VGNN) to predict phonon spectra and bandstructures directly from atomic coordinates, addressing challenges of variable-length output and complex unit cells. It presents three variants—vector virtual nodes (VVN), matrix virtual nodes (MVN), and momentum-dependent matrix virtual nodes (k-MVN)—to predict Γ-point phonons and full dispersion. The method is validated on alloy systems and used to build a Γ-phonon database of over 146,000 materials from the Materials Project.

title: JARVIS-Leaderboard: a large scale benchmark of materials design methods
research_summary: This work introduces JARVIS-Leaderboard, an open-source and community-driven platform that facilitates benchmarking and enhances reproducibility for materials design methods across multiple categories: Artificial Intelligence (AI), Electronic Structure (ES), Force-fields (FF), Quantum Computation (QC), and Experiments (EXP). It enables users to set up benchmarks with custom tasks and contributions in the form of dataset, code, and metadata submissions, covering various data modalities including atomic structures, spectra, images, and text. The platform includes 1281 contributions to 274 benchmarks using 152 methods with more than 8 million data points.

title: Structure-based out-of-distribution (OOD) materials property prediction: a benchmark study
research_summary: This paper presents a comprehensive benchmark study evaluating graph neural networks (GNNs) for predicting materials properties on out-of-distribution (OOD) test sets—materials whose structures or properties deviate significantly from the training distribution. It introduces five OOD test set generation methods (LOCO, SparseXsingle, SparseYsingle, SparseXcluster, SparseYcluster) applied to three MatBench datasets (dielectric, elasticity, perovskites), and benchmarks eight SOTA GNNs. The study reveals a substantial generalization gap: current top-performing GNNs underperform dramatically on OOD tasks compared to their i.i.d. MatBench baselines, identifying CGCNN, ALIGNN, and DeeperGATGNN as comparatively robust. It further analyzes latent physical spaces to explain performance differences and advocates for domain adaptation and physics-informed modeling to improve OOD generalization.

title: A Recipe for Charge Density Prediction
research_summary: This paper proposes a machine learning method to predict the electronic charge density of atomic systems — a core quantity in density functional theory (DFT) from which all ground-state physicochemical properties can be derived. It addresses the accuracy–efficiency trade-off by introducing three key ingredients: (1) an orbital-based representation augmented with virtual orbitals placed at bond midpoints; (2) expressive, learnable even-tempered Gaussian basis sets with trainable orbital exponents; and (3) a high-capacity SE(3)-equivariant neural network architecture (eSCN). The method is evaluated on the QM9 charge density dataset and achieves state-of-the-art accuracy while being over 30× faster than prior methods.

title: Learning Superconductivity from Ordered and Disordered Material Structures
research_summary: The paper introduces SuperCon3D, a new dataset containing both 3D crystal structures (ordered and disordered) and experimental superconducting transition temperatures (Tc), and proposes two deep learning models: SODNet for screening known structures to predict Tc, and DiffCSP-SC for generating novel high-Tc superconductor candidates. It validates both models experimentally and presents candidate materials for future experimental validation.

title: How simple can you go? An off-the-shelf transformer approach to molecular dynamics
file_name: 32_How simple can you go - An off-the-shelf transformer approach to molecular dynamics.pdf
research_summary: This paper presents MD-ET, an edge transformer adapted for molecular dynamics with minimal physical inductive biases (no built-in rotational equivariance or energy conservation), trained on the QCML dataset. It evaluates performance on benchmarks (QCML, MD17, Ko2020, xxMD, SPICE), analyzes approximate equivariance and energy conservation, and assesses stability and faithfulness of NVE and NVT simulations.

title: Study on bandgap predications of ABX3-type perovskites by machine learning
file_name: 33_Study on bandgap predications of ABX3-type perovskites by machine learning.pdf
research_summary: This paper develops machine learning models to predict the experimental bandgaps of ABX3-type perovskites using 227 experimentally measured bandgap values collected from 1254 publications. It evaluates 24 model variants across 4 databases and 6 algorithms, identifies Xgboost and MLP as top performers, validates predictions against new experimental synthesis and DFT calculations, and uses SHAP to interpret chemical composition effects—finding B-site metal and X-site halogen ions dominate bandgap control, consistent with B–X bond length and angle physics.

title: Physics-Informed Weakly Supervised Learning for Interatomic Potentials
file_name: 34_Physics-Informed Weakly Supervised Learning for Interatomic Potentials.pdf
research_summary: We address this challenge by introducing a physics-informed, weakly supervised approach for training machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs). We introduce two novel loss functions, extrapolating the potential energy via a Taylor expansion and using the concept of conservative forces. Our approach improves the accuracy of MLIPs applied to training tasks with sparse training data sets and reduces the need for pre-training computationally demanding models with large data sets.

title: Correcting DFT formation energies towards experimental accuracy using foundational MLIPs and latent-feature delta-learning
file_name: 35_Correcting DFT formation energies towards experimental accuracy using foundational MLIPs and latent-feature delta-learning.pdf
research_summary: The paper introduces thermodynamic stability data for the Materials Cloud three-dimensional crystals database (MC3D) and validates it against other DFT databases. It then improves agreement of DFT formation energies with experimental formation enthalpies by first using zero-shot foundational machine learning interatomic potentials (fMLIPs) trained at the r2SCAN level (PET-OMATPES), reducing mean absolute error (MAE) by >40% relative to GGA without additional DFT calculations. Finally, it trains classical ML models (KRR, RF, GPR) in a delta-learning framework on latent features from PET-OMATPES to further correct formation energies, achieving MAE <50 meV/atom — comparable to experimental uncertainty — while limiting distortion of relative phase stability via regularization.

title: Accelerating the Discovery of Hybrid Perovskites with Targeted Band Gaps via Interpretable Machine Learning
file_name: 36_Accelerating the Discovery of Hybrid Perovskites with Targeted Band Gaps via Interpretable Machine Learning.pdf
research_summary: This study developed an interpretable machine learning strategy combining feature engineering, gradient-boosted regression tree (GBRT), and genetic algorithm-based symbolic regression (GASR) to predict the experimental band gaps of hybrid organic–inorganic perovskites (HOIPs) and quantitatively interpret the physical factors affecting band gaps. It identified χB−X as the most important feature and derived the formula Eg = χB−X² + 0.881χB−X. The model screened and experimentally validated three novel HOIP compositions, including MA₀.₂₃FA₀.₀₂Cs₀.₇₅Pb₀.₅₉Sn₀.₄₁Br₀.₂₄I₂.₇₆ with a targeted band gap of 1.39 eV.

title: Assessing data-driven predictions of band gap and electrical conductivity for transparent conducting materials
file_name: 37_Assessing data-driven predictions of band gap and electrical conductivity for transparent conducting materials.pdf
research_summary: This paper proposes a data-driven framework to accelerate the discovery of new transparent conducting materials (TCMs) by predicting band gap and electrical conductivity from stoichiometry alone, using experimentally validated datasets and state-of-the-art ML models evaluated via bespoke methods including leave-one-TCM-family-out to assess ability to identify previously unseen TCM families.

title: Rational design of nanoscale stabilized oxide catalysts for OER with OC22
file_name: 38_Rational design of nanoscale stabilized oxide catalysts for OER with OC22.pdf
research_summary: This work uses pre-trained OC22 machine learning models to interpolate total energy predictions for OER surface intermediates on 4119 oxide materials, then constructs a flexible high-throughput screening framework to identify viable anode catalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) under bulk and nanoscale Pourbaix stability, material cost, overpotential, and metastability constraints — identifying 122 bulk and 68 nanoscale candidates.

title: A foundation machine learning potential with polarizable long-range interactions for materials modelling
file_name: 39_A foundation machine learning potential with polarizable long-range interactions for materials modelling.pdf
research_summary: We present a foundation framework that integrates explicit polarizable long-range physics with an equivariant graph neural network potential. It employs a physically motivated polarizable charge equilibration scheme that directly optimizes electrostatic interaction energies rather than partial charges. The foundation model, trained across the periodic table up to Pu, demonstrates strong performance across key materials modeling challenges. It effectively captures long-range interactions that are challenging for traditional message-passing mechanisms and accurately reproduces polarization effects under external electric fields. We have applied the model to mechanical properties, ionic diffusivity in solid-state electrolytes, ferroelectric phase transitions, and reactive dynamics at electrode-electrolyte interfaces, highlighting the model’s capacity to balance accuracy and computational efficiency. Furthermore, we show that as a foundation model, it can be efficiently finetuned to achieve high-level accuracy for specific challenging systems.

title: Atomic-scale revelation of in situ reverse regulation from particles to clusters in the Ni/La-CeOx catalyst
file_name: 40_Atomic-scale revelation of in situ reverse regulation from particles to clusters in the Ni-La-CeOx catalyst.pdf
research_summary: This study proposes and demonstrates a reverse regulation strategy—from metal particles to subnanometer clusters—enabled by rational design of catalytic environment and metal-support interaction, overcoming classical sintering limitations at high temperature. Using in situ characterization and theoretical calculations, it reveals atomic migration pathways and thermodynamic steady-state reconstruction underlying stable Ni cluster formation on La-doped CeO₂.

title: An open-access database and analysis tool for perovskite solar cells based on the FAIR data principles
file_name: 42_An open-access database and analysis tool for perovskite solar cells based on the FAIR data principles.pdf
research_summary: This paper describes the creation of an open-access, FAIR-compliant database for metal-halide perovskite solar cell device data, containing over 42,400 devices extracted manually from peer-reviewed literature. It includes development of interactive web-based tools for exploration, analysis, filtering, and visualization; establishment of metadata ontology and data extraction protocols; and demonstration of analytical insights (e.g., efficiency trends, HTL impact on Voc, bandgap-composition relationships). The project aims to transform perovskite research data management by enabling community-wide data sharing, reuse, and AI/ML readiness.

title: Machine learning for improved density functional theory thermodynamics
file_name: 43_Machine learning for improved density functional theory thermodynamics.pdf
research_summary: This work presents a machine learning approach to systematically correct intrinsic energy resolution errors in density functional theory (DFT) calculations of alloy formation enthalpies, improving reliability for ternary phase stability predictions. A neural network model is trained to predict the discrepancy between DFT-calculated and experimentally measured enthalpies for binary and ternary alloys and compounds, using elemental concentrations, atomic numbers, and interaction terms as features. The model is validated on Al–Ni–Pd and Al–Ni–Ti systems.
